a: Unscoped grids resolve a tagged pitch with the unit's offset; scoped grids subtract it
With `bounds`, the grid layer emits every line across the bounds, not just the visible part
Grid line and clip coordinates are written as world-space Float32, so lines far from the origin snap to float32 steps
useGridCellHover keeps a stale cell when the view, spacing or regions change without a pointer move
sceneGridRegions builds its child lists by copying the array for every node, quadratic in sibling containers, on every paint and pointermove
b: Grid lines and clip outlines are written as absolute world coordinates in a Float32Array with no `origin`, so they land off their positions far from world zero
Without `scopes`, a tagged grid length is read with its unit's offset, so a unit with an affine offset moves the pitch; with `scopes` the same length is read offset-free
A NaN or infinite `offset` passes validation and `cellOf` returns a cell of NaNs instead of `null`
`useGridCellHover` reads `ref.current` once per effect run, so an element attached after mount, or swapped for another, never gets listeners
